notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45451877/881fe762bc10827416f89c6839067bff8fa1b118.jpg[/img]

Now that you've played a few rounds and want to level up, here’s a pro tip you should try right away!
Don’t Overestimate Suited Cards:
Suited cards are two cards of the same suit (like hearts, diamonds, etc.). 
A lot of players think they’re always a good bet because they could make a flush. 
But here’s the thing: low suited cards, like 7-2, aren’t as strong as they seem.

Sure, sometimes you might hit that flush, but in the long run, you'll probably end up losing more chips than you win if you keep chasing them. 
So, don’t get too excited just because your cards are suited.

Pro Tip: It's better to focus on stronger hands and think carefully about whether to call, raise, or fold.

notes.title: Insider Tips
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45451877/cd6ff77959cac02638fcc318db162be06c5c30da.jpg[/img]
ːsteamthumbsupː Manage Your Bankroll: 
Your bankroll is the money you have set aside for playing poker. Never risk all your bankroll on one table or tournament. Instead, only risk, at most, 5% of your bankroll at a time. And if you lose that, have the discipline to walk away. This ensures there’s always money left over for tomorrow. 

ːsteamthumbsupː Avoid Common Mistakes: 
Some common mistakes include playing too many hands, ignoring position, not watching opponents carefully, bluffing too often, and not being prepared to cut your losses and fold when necessary.
